exercise.name: Smith Reverse Grip Bent Over Row

reference.title: Smith Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Brace in the hinge, breathe out as the bar comes up, in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, short squeeze, 2 s down
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: keep the trunk still with no heave, about 2 reps in reserve.
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep touches the belly without the trunk rising.

cues.text: Set the pegs at about knee height. Underhand grip about shoulder width, turn the bar off the pegs, knees soft, hinge until the trunk is about 30-40 degrees above the floor, back flat, bar hanging under the shoulders.
Drive the elbows back close to the sides and pull the bar to the lower belly.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together for a moment; the trunk stays still.
Lower the bar slowly down the rails to straight arms.
Keep the hinge and the brace; start the next rep without standing up. After the last rep stand up and turn the bar back onto the pegs.

mistakes.mistake: Standing up and heaving the bar
mistakes.fix: Fix the trunk angle; lighten the load until it stays still.
Keep the elbows close to the body and drive them toward the hips.

mistakes.mistake: Curling the bar with the biceps
mistakes.fix: Think of pulling with the elbows; the hands are just hooks.
Chest proud, brace, hinge only as far as a flat back allows.

kinematics.norm: Bent-over rows load the lumbar spine and extensors; the trunk is held still (Fenwick 2009); about 30-45 degrees above horizontal is common

kinematics.peak: ≈105°, elbows 7.6 cm out from the shoulders, bar at the lower belly; shoulder blades retracted (clavicle protraction 6° to -14°)
kinematics.norm: Underhand grip keeps the elbows close and brings in the biceps (Lehman 2004 compared grips in lat exercises)

kinematics.peak: 1.1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down, 1.2 s reset
kinematics.norm: About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Smith rails 1.7° from vertical (top toward the back), bar 81.7 cm high at the top
kinematics.peak: 52.6 cm at the bottom (29.1 cm along the rails); hands' midpoint within 0.03 cm of the rail line at every key
kinematics.norm: Fixed by the guide rails: the bar can only travel along them (here a rail line fitted to the free-bar path, a few degrees from vertical at most); the bar runs to the lower belly (common coaching)

cautions: Set the safety stops just under the lowest bar position before the first rep; the bar cannot go lower than them.
Practise turning the bar on and off the pegs (a small turn of the wrists) with an empty bar first.
The rails fix the bar path: place yourself so the movement feels natural for the joints, and do not force range.
Hold the brace and the hinge for the whole set; rack the bar if the back starts to round.
Elbow or biceps pain with the underhand grip: use an overhand grip.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lower back tires: more upright trunk or chest-supported row.
regressions: Overhand barbell row with a lighter load.
progressions: Pendlay-style dead stop from the floor.

muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the elbows back close to the body; the underhand grip keeps the arm path close (Lehman 2004).
